Chapter 4: The Five Commandments of Fastlane Entrepreneurship
Let’s dive into what really sets Fastlane businesses apart—and no, it’s not just luck or a sudden stroke of genius.
It’s about following a handful of powerful principles, kind of like having a compass for every opportunity you come across.
These are known as the Five Commandments, and they act as filters, making sure you’re spending your energy on ideas with real potential.
First up is Need.
Your business has to solve a genuine problem or meet an urgent desire. Think about it—are you addressing what people actually want or just what you find interesting? The best opportunities come from easing pain points or fulfilling desires that are felt by a lot of people, not just a select few.
Next, there’s Entry.
Here’s something to pay attention to: if anyone can copy your business overnight, it’s probably not going to lead to lasting success. You’ll want some real barriers to entry—maybe it’s specialized knowledge, access to unique resources, or a fresh approach that’s tough to imitate.
The third commandment is Control.
You need to have the reins on the key parts of your business. If you’re dependent on another platform, a trend, or a third party, you’re at their mercy—and that’s risky. Real control means you own your product, your process, and the relationship with your customers.
Now, let’s talk about Scale.
Your business should have the potential to reach a wide audience. Maybe that’s through digital channels, franchising, or another way to multiply your reach. If your idea is limited by location, your own time, or how many people you can serve personally, it’s going to have a tough time hitting Fastlane levels.
And finally, there’s Time.
The goal here is to set things up so your income isn’t stuck to the hours you work. That means building systems, automating what you can, and delegating smartly. Imagine creating a machine that keeps earning—even while you sleep or take a vacation.
When you use these commandments to check your ideas, you’ll quickly spot the difference between something that just sounds cool and something that can really work.
Think about it: a local coffee shop? Sure, it meets a need and offers some control, but it’s tough to scale and hard to separate income from your time.
On the other hand, if you build an online platform that connects providers and customers, you can reach people worldwide—and it can run 24/7.
These principles are all about value creation. Instead of chasing trends or copying what others are doing, Fastlane entrepreneurs look for unmet needs and find unique, scalable ways to serve them. They focus on building assets that can grow and evolve, rather than jumping on short-lived opportunities.
And remember, these commandments aren’t strict rules—they’re more like guiding lights.
They help you focus on what’s really important, and avoid those common traps—like starting something that’s easy but impossible to sustain, or chasing excitement instead of real potential.
